evidence.quote:
one takes a small chunk of
blubber, thus, and thus makes it hollow.
title=""  Then into the
hollow goes the whalebone, so, tightly coiled, and another piece
of blubber is fitted over the whale-bone.
title=""  After that it is
put outside where it freezes into a little round ball.
evidence.paraphrase: Keesh explains the mechanism of his hunting device: a coiled whalebone encased in blubber that freezes into a ball.

evidence.quote:
The bear swallows the little round ball, the blubber melts, the
whalebone with its sharp ends stands out straight, the bear gets
sick, and when the bear is very sick, why, you kill him with a
spear.
evidence.paraphrase: Keesh describes how the swallowed device works inside the bear, disabling it so it can be killed.

evidence.quote:
it was determined to put spies on his track when he
went forth to hunt, so that his methods might be learned.
evidence.paraphrase: The council decides to observe Keesh secretly to discover the method behind his hunting success.

evidence.quote:
I have but devised a means
whereby I may kill the ice-bear with ease, that is all.
title=""  It
be headcraft, not witchcraft.
evidence.paraphrase: Keesh contrasts his rational invented method with the supernatural explanation others assumed.

evidence.quote:
He hunts with evil spirits,
title="" some of the people
contended, "wherefore his hunting is rewarded.
title=""  How
else can it be, save that he hunts with evil spirits?
evidence.paraphrase: Villagers react to Keesh's success by attributing it to witchcraft or spirits.

evidence.quote:
The men could not bring
themselves to believe that the boy Keesh, single-handed, had
accomplished so great a marvel.
evidence.paraphrase: The men doubt that a boy could have killed dangerous bears alone.

evidence.quote:
Because he exercised headcraft and not
witchcraft, he rose from the meanest igloo to be head man
of his village
evidence.paraphrase: Keesh's inventive method transforms his social status from poorest to leader.
